name: Red Fort (Lal Qila)
path: Red Fort (Lal Qila), Central Delhi, India
summary: Historic 17th-century Mughal imperial palace citadel built of red sandstone by Emperor Shah Jahan.
points: Commissioned in 1638 CE by Emperor Shah Jahan; completed 1648 CE
Mughal dynasty; designated UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007
Venue of India's annual Independence Day flag-hoisting address by the Prime Minister

name: Qutub Minar & Iron Pillar
path: Qutub Minar & Iron Pillar, South Delhi, India
summary: 73-meter soaring minaret of victory and rust-resistant 4th-century Gupta iron pillar.
points: Construction started in 1199 CE by Qutb-ud-din Aibak and completed by Iltutmish; Delhi Sultanate (Mamluk dynasty)
Inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993
Houses the 1,600-year-old Gupta Iron Pillar that has never rusted

name: India Gate
summary: Ceremonial 42-meter triumphal arch war memorial designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens.
points: Foundation laid in 1921, inaugurated in 1931 by Viceroy Lord Irwin
Designed by Edwin Lutyens; honors 84,000 soldiers who died in World War I
Features the Amar Jawan Jyoti eternal flame and National War Memorial

name: Swaminarayan Akshardham
summary: World's largest comprehensive Hindu temple complex, carved entirely from pink sandstone and Carrara marble.
points: Consecrated on 6 November 2005 by Pramukh Swami Maharaj
Built without structural steel according to ancient Shilpa Shastras featuring 20,000 carved statues

name: Lotus Temple (Bahá'í House of Worship)
path: Lotus Temple (Bahá'í House of Worship), South Delhi, India
summary: Architectural masterpiece shaped like a blossoming 27-petal white marble lotus flower.
points: Completed in 1986, designed by Iranian-Canadian architect Fariborz Sahba
Bahá'í faith; open to people of all religions and denominations for silent contemplation
Won numerous international architectural awards for expressionist concrete shell design
